header_summary:
A new protocol synthesizing elements from established consensus mechanisms, including features reminiscent of the Snowball protocol, has been proposed to facilitate pre-block soft-agreement within the Bitcoin mempool. By enabling batch agreement on groups of transactions prior to block discovery, this approach aims to accelerate block propagation and improve machine efficiency across the network, with further technical details available in the original research paper ([source](https://beige-worrying-unicorn-969.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/bafybeigsbdid4znwtmoqh55yid2etxkujci33dzqt3ia6bt5vwsnllfqym), [discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/snowball-to-snowstorm/3014)).

Recent comparative experiments by Aaron Recompilé examined three Bitcoin state channel update mechanisms—APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV ladder, and TEMPLATEHASH+CSFS+INTERNALKEY—demonstrating that the latest TEMPLATEHASH-based approach achieves significantly reduced script complexity and witness size. Detailed code examples and transaction sequences illustrate the technical distinctions and advantages, with resources available for further review ([templatehash.py](https://github.com/aaron-recompile/btcaaron/blob/5ef4cb3dff5d51d812ff55a134d48c0e269323e7/btcaaron/templatehash.py), [discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-third-time-templatehash-csfs-internalkey/3012)).

The Bitcoin development archive interface has been enhanced by introducing a "Years" navigation feature, offering users a clear chronological organization of threads since 2011 and improved monthly access. Renaming and redesigning the navigation, along with the addition of a “Recently active” list, significantly streamlines the process of locating discussions from specific periods and reflects ongoing user-driven improvements ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/we-made-the-bitcoin-dev-mailing-list-readable-15-years-24-699-messages/2985/3)).

recent_posts.title: Snowball to Snowstorm
recent_posts.summary: - A new protocol enables soft-agreement in the Bitcoin mempool to improve block propagation speed.  - It facilitates batch agreement on transaction groups using a consensus inspired by the Snowball protocol.  - This method streamlines block formation, reduces selection redundancies, and enhances network coordination.

recent_posts.title: Eltoo state chain on signet, third time: TEMPLATEHASH + CSFS + INTERNALKEY
recent_posts.summary: - Three methods were compared for updating multi-party channels using APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV, and TEMPLATEHASH.  - TEMPLATEHASH provided the smallest update leaf, constant witness size, and enabled more flexible scripting.  - Technical differences impact transaction count, witness size, and script complexity among the approaches.

recent_posts.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
recent_posts.summary: - The archive now features a structured "Years" section listing every year since 2011 with thread counts.  - Each year page allows users to navigate months via anchor-linked headings for efficient browsing.  - The homepage includes a "Recently active" list, and navigation has improved clarity with renaming and enhancements.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - Node configuration changes, such as increased inbound connections and mempool policies, significantly influenced block reconstruction efficiency.  - Periods of high mempool activity led to decreased reconstruction rates without additional transaction requests on several nodes.  - Enabling mempoolfullrbf improved block propagation, suggesting policy changes could further optimize reconstruction network-wide.

active_posts.title: What is the importance of running a node?
active_posts.summary: - Widespread support for running nodes faces reluctance due to unclear personal benefits and feasibility.  - Critics question the actual security improvements and tangible advantages of operating a node for individuals.  - Practical barriers and lack of compelling reasons hinder universal adoption and leave the debate unresolved.

active_posts.title: Thoughts on a network policy for quantum-vulnerable UTXOs (long-exposure quantum attacks)
active_posts.summary: - Address type and re-use vulnerabilities require targeted strategies such as freezing transactions or imposing rate-limits.  - For re-use vulnerabilities, proposals include permitting spending or instituting temporary freezes pending secure recovery solutions.  - The timing of these protective measures is crucial to avoid either unfair penalties or widespread theft.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP - Block size doubles at each reward halving with max block size of 32M
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The proposal recommends doubling the maximum block size at each block subsidy halving until 32MB.  - The goal is to restore the original 32MB default, providing a prudent, long-term scalability approach.  - Legacy clients would become incompatible, causing a network split when blocks exceed 1MB.

today_in_history_posts.title: Lightning, the death of BIP62, and Segregated Witness
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Anchor malleability was identified as an issue, and BIP62 would not solve it.  - Four solutions were considered, but assuming Segregated Witness would address malleability was chosen.  - This decision simplifies lightning code and aligns with Bitcoin and smart contract system goals.

today_in_history_posts.title: Batched Splicing Considered Risky
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Splicing transactions introduce risks, especially due to absent disincentives for disruption and potential double-spending attacks.  - Operational complexity and trust issues increase when mitigating these vulnerabilities, particularly in zero-confirmation situations.  - Batched splicing is considered risky, especially with disruptive peers or insufficient reserve funds in channels.
